q: How do I import files?
a: File ▸ Import… (`file.import`) takes files or whole folders. Caption files (.srt, .vtt, .scc) become caption tracks, and numbered stills can come in as one image sequence (a preference). For a camera card, copy it first with the verified copy and import from the copy.

q: Can I import a numbered image sequence as one clip?
a: File ▸ Import… (`file.import`) takes files or whole folders. Caption files (.srt, .vtt, .scc) become caption tracks, and numbered stills can come in as one image sequence (a preference). For a camera card, copy it first with the verified copy and import from the copy.

q: In Resolve I'd import on the Media page. Where do I import here?
a: File ▸ Import… (`file.import`) for files or folders; for camera cards, use the verified card copy first and import from the copy.

q: What generated media can I make?
a: File ▸ New makes items that need no file: Bars and Tone (a test signal), Black Video, Color Matte (a flat colour), a Universal Counting Leader, Transparent Video (an empty clip to hold effects) and an Adjustment Layer, a clip whose effects apply to everything below it so one grade or blur covers many clips.

q: What is Transparent Video for?

q: In Resolve I'd use an adjustment clip. What's the Revolution version?
a: File ▸ New ▸ Adjustment Layer (`file.newAdjustmentLayer`): put it on a track above the clips; its effects (a grade, a blur) apply to everything below it.

q: In Premiere I'd add an Adjustment Layer. Same here?
a: File ▸ New ▸ Adjustment Layer (`file.newAdjustmentLayer`): put it on a track above the clips; its effects (a grade, a blur) apply to everything below it.

q: In Resolve I'd make Media Pool bins. How do I do that here?
a: New ▸ Bin (`file.newBin`) makes a folder in the Project panel (Media Pool in the Resolve workflow); drag items in or use `project.moveToBin`.

q: How do I go back to my last save?
a: Revert (`file.revert`) goes back to the last save. After a crash or power cut, the next launch offers Recover Unsaved Changes… (`file.recover`) from Revolution's journal of unsaved changes; `file.discardRecovery` throws them away.

q: How do I throw away recovered changes?

q: What does the offline slate mean?
a: A clip whose file can't be found shows the offline slate. Link Media… (`media.linkMedia`; agents use `media.relink`) points it at the file's new place, checking size and a content fingerprint so the wrong file isn't accepted. Make Offline / Offline All disconnect media on purpose; Replace Footage… swaps an item's file keeping every clip and its edits.

q: How do I relink one clip?
a: A clip whose file can't be found shows the offline slate. Link Media… (`media.linkMedia`; agents use `media.relink`) points it at the file's new place, checking size and a content fingerprint so the wrong file isn't accepted. Make Offline / Offline All disconnect media on purpose; Replace Footage… swaps an item's file keeping every clip and its edits.

q: In Premiere I'd use Link Media. Does that work here?
a: Use Link Media… (`media.linkMedia`) on the offline items and point it at the files' new place; Revolution checks each candidate is the same file before accepting it.

q: In Resolve I'd use Relink Selected Clips. What's the equivalent?
a: Use Link Media… (`media.linkMedia`) on the offline items and point it at the files' new place; Revolution checks each candidate is the same file before accepting it.

q: What are the time interpolation options?
a: `clip.setTimeInterpolation` sets how in-between frames are made for speed changes: frame sampling (repeats frames, crisp but steppy), frame blending (mixes neighbours, smoother but soft) or optical flow (makes new frames from motion, smoothest, can warp fast movement). Frame Hold (`clip.frameHold`) freezes a clip on a frame. Link ties picture and sound together; Group makes several clips select together (`clip.ungroup` undoes it).

q: How do I fit a clip of a different size to the sequence?
a: Scale to Frame Size (`clip.scaleToFrameSize`) fits a clip of another size to the sequence; Reveal in Project (`clip.revealInProject`) shows its item in the Project panel.

q: How do I find a timeline clip's item in the project?
a: Scale to Frame Size (`clip.scaleToFrameSize`) fits a clip of another size to the sequence; Reveal in Project (`clip.revealInProject`) shows its item in the Project panel.

q: How does Scene Edit Detection decide what is a cut?
a: It compares every frame with the one before, in the background; Sensitivity (0–100, default 50) decides how big a change counts as a cut, and shots shorter than six frames are ignored. On each change it can apply a cut (default), create subclips and / or generate markers; each result is one undo step.

q: Are very short shots detected?

On each change it can apply a cut (default), create subclips and / or generate markers; each result is one undo step.

q: In Resolve I'd use the Scene Cut Detector. What's the equivalent here?
a: Select the clip on the timeline and choose Clip ▸ Scene Edit Detection… (`clip.sceneEditDetection`): it finds the cuts and applies them, makes subclips or adds markers.

q: How do I extract a clip's audio to its own file?
a: Breakout to Mono (`clip.breakoutToMono`) makes a mono clip per channel, so a two-microphone recording becomes two clips you can level separately. Extract Audio (`clip.extractAudio`) writes a clip's sound to its own file. Modify ▸ Audio Channels… (Shift+G) maps source channels as stereo, mono or picked channels.

q: Which timeline exchange formats can Revolution export?
a: EDL (`file.exportEdl`: simple conform, one video track of cuts, loses effects and most tracks), FCPXML (`file.exportFcpxml`: Final Cut Pro and apps that read it, including Resolve; effects don't carry over), OpenTimelineIO (`file.exportOtio`: open pipelines; newer, support varies), and AAF import (`file.importAaf`) for edits or sound sessions from Avid or Premiere.

q: What is OpenTimelineIO good for?

q: In Premiere I start on the Home screen. What's the equivalent?
a: The Project Manager: a full-window screen of project tiles (New Project first, Open / Close at the bottom right), shown at launch in the Resolve workflow. It plays the part of Premiere's Home screen and recent projects list.

q: In Resolve I'd use the Project Manager. Is it the same?
a: The Project Manager: a full-window screen of project tiles (New Project first, Open / Close at the bottom right), shown at launch in the Resolve workflow. It plays the part of Premiere's Home screen and recent projects list.

q: What is Other locations in the Project Manager?
a: Folders inside the projects folder are the Project Manager's folders. Projects you opened from somewhere else are listed under Other locations at the top level; a moved or deleted one shows greyed as Missing.

q: Do folders in the projects folder show up?
a: Folders inside the projects folder are the Project Manager's folders. Projects you opened from somewhere else are listed under Other locations at the top level; a moved or deleted one shows greyed as Missing.

q: What page do I land on after creating a project?
a: The new project is saved as `<name>.fcproj` in the folder you're looking at, opened, and you land on the Edit page. If the project you had open has unsaved changes, Revolution asks first: Save, Don't Save or Cancel.

q: What if my open project has unsaved changes when I make a new one?
a: The new project is saved as `<name>.fcproj` in the folder you're looking at, opened, and you land on the Edit page. If the project you had open has unsaved changes, Revolution asks first: Save, Don't Save or Cancel.

q: Which page does a project open on?
a: Double-click a tile (or select it and press Enter, or click Open). The project opens on the page it was last saved on (Edit if unknown). Close (or Esc) goes back to the project you had open; with none open, the Project Manager stays.

q: How do I close the Project Manager without opening anything?
a: Double-click a tile (or select it and press Enter, or click Open). The project opens on the page it was last saved on (Edit if unknown). Close (or Esc) goes back to the project you had open; with none open, the Project Manager stays.

q: How do I switch the Project Manager to a list view?
a: Use the grid and list buttons in the row under the title (the list shows name, dates, resolution, frame rate and timelines); Info shows the selected project's details; New folder (`projects.newFolder`) makes a folder. Agents get the same listing with `projects.list`.

q: How do I make a folder for projects?
a: Use the grid and list buttons in the row under the title (the list shows name, dates, resolution, frame rate and timelines); Info shows the selected project's details; New folder (`projects.newFolder`) makes a folder. Agents get the same listing with `projects.list`.

q: How do I show a project file in my file manager?
a: Right-click its tile: Duplicate makes "<name> copy" next to it; Reveal in File Manager shows the file; Rename… renames the file (not the open project); Move to Trash… asks, then moves it to the system trash. Under Other locations, Remove from List forgets a project without touching the file.

q: What does Import do with a .fcproj file?
a: Import (`projects.import`) copies a `.fcproj` file into the folder you're looking at (a second copy gets a number, nothing is overwritten); agents can import a whole exported archive folder by path. If clips show offline after importing on another computer, use Link Media… and point it at the archive's media.

q: My imported project's clips are offline. What now?

q: Where is Media Management in the Resolve workflow?
a: The collect / consolidate tool (Premiere's Project Manager) is File ▸ Media Management… in the Resolve workflow, the same command `file.projectManager`.
